title: Trace Before Run
user: Beginning programming students who can write fragments of Python but struggle to apply logic and debug simple problems.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ask HN discussion about introducing a 13-year-old to programming emphasizes logic, branching, loops, decomposition, debugging, and self-correction before language preference.
A Python learner directly reports difficulty applying logical thinking to basic exercises and homework.

recurrence: A learner and an independent parent/educator discussion in 2025 point to the same early-stage transfer problem: syntax exposure does not create tracing or decomposition habits.
current_workaround: Watch tutorials, ask an LLM for the answer, repeatedly run code, or copy solutions from practice sites.
incumbents_and_gap: Python Tutor visualizes executions and coding platforms grade answers; the unresolved gap is a quick prediction-first drill where learners commit to a trace before seeing output.
smallest_useful_product: Static browser game with short editable Python-like snippets, variable-table prediction, branch-path selection, reveal-after-commit, and original micro-puzzles. Non-goals: code execution for arbitrary input, accounts, ranking, or an AI hint bot.
success_measure: After five sessions, 60% of test learners improve at least 20 percentage points on an unseen five-item trace quiz.
monetization: free — an open, linkable drill works best for teachers assigning it without procurement.
constraints: Use a restricted hand-authored grammar rather than executing user code; meet keyboard and color-contrast requirements.
why_distinct: Prediction before execution is the product mechanic; it is neither a generic code playground nor an answer-generating tutor.
summary: Predict Python traces before you run them
